rationale: The hack has one root cause: the policy can read what the grader will check. Moving tests/ into a verifier-only stage removes the answer key from the agent's reachable filesystem; dropping the solution/ COPY removes the oracle. Re-generating expected values per episode (LF-003) means that even a leaked literal is worthless next episode, so the fix survives future packaging mistakes. Task semantics are unchanged: an honest solution passes exactly as before.

changes.before: Anything readable from the container filesystem
changes.rationale: The policy could read /tests and /opt/solution. The agent container now exposes /app only.

changes.before: Expected outputs in tests/ (intended, but reachable — see findings)
changes.after: Expected outputs in tests/ (verifier stage only; never mounted in the agent container)
changes.rationale: tests/ moves from a bind mount at start to a COPY in the verifier build stage.

changes.before: Reference solve.sh per task (intended, but shipped in the image)
changes.after: Reference solve.sh per task (not in the image; solution/ is in .dockerignore)
changes.rationale: The oracle solutions were left in the image by a debugging COPY line.

changes.after: Tests: copied into the verifier stage at verify time
variant_regen · fresh expected values per episode
changes.rationale: Seven tasks graded on a single literal. Regenerating the expected value per episode makes a leaked literal worthless.

changes.before: tests/test_outputs.py asserts a fixed literal (1843 rows)
changes.after: tests/test_outputs.py asserts against a per-episode variant (see diff)
changes.rationale: The code-level change; the unified diff shows it in full.

allow: Read task instruction.md and anything under /app
Run and inspect its own code, stdout, stderr
Install the two packages pinned in requirements.txt
Iterate on failures from its own test runs
deny: Read or list /tests at any point in the episode
Learn literal expected values — variants regenerate per episode
